I farm this year for steadiness, not for chasing the highest possible yield. I am 78, my land is only 3 mu, and there are just two people in the household, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on the full 3 mu and use simple, proven management that fits my labor and my well irrigation. For winter wheat, I will use an improved variety, put fertilizer in at a moderate level, and plan on two irrigations because wheat in south Hebei responds clearly to key spring water, while too much water and fertilizer just raise cost and risk. For summer maize, I will switch on the same 3 mu to a hybrid, direct-seed after wheat, keep fertilizer moderate, and usually irrigate once at the key stage if rain is not enough, because maize here gets more summer rain than wheat. I will also keep pesticide work to the essential passes only, mainly one weed-control pass and one disease-insect control pass, because at my age I want stable output with less wasted work. This is broadly aligned with recent Ministry of Agriculture fertilization guidance for Hebei’s winter wheat and Huanghuaihai summer maize, Hebei’s 2025 wheat yield level, and North China irrigation findings showing wheat benefits from 1 to 2 key irrigations while summer maize is more rain-matched: https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/2023/202309/t20230928_6437567.htm , https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/ZZYGLS/202303/t20230314_6423039.htm , https://wenwu.hebei.gov.cn/system/2025/07/12/030350574.shtml , https://www.engineering.org.cn/sscae/CN/1160079841619927252 , https://zwxb.chinacrops.org/CN/10.3724/SP.J.1006.2019.81060
